questions.stem: A colleague wants every user whose department attribute equals "Finance" to be added to a group. They have started building a Workflows flow. What should you tell them?
options: Use a scheduled flow that scans all users nightly
Use an Event Hook so the logic runs outside Okta
Use a Group Rule instead; it is declarative, faster and has nothing to monitor
Continue in Workflows, because attribute-based membership needs a flow
questions.explanation: Attribute-based group membership is exactly what Group Rules are for. A flow would re-implement a built-in feature, cost an active-flow slot, and give you an execution history to babysit. Workflows earns its place when you need multiple steps, external systems, waiting or retries.

questions.stem: A helper flow in your folder shows no on/off toggle and nothing in its Execution History. Which statement is true?
options: Helper flows only run when another flow calls them; it simply has not been called yet
It is broken and must be re-imported
Execution History is not kept for helper flows
Helper flows run on a schedule and this one has not fired
questions.explanation: A helper flow has no trigger of its own. It is inactive until a parent flow invokes it with Call Flow, Call Flow Async, or a list card such as For Each. Once it has run, its executions appear in its own Execution History, which is where you debug failures inside loops.

questions.stem: A flow needs to pause a token-minting transaction and inject a claim based on an external lookup. Which mechanism is the fit, and what is the main constraint?
options: A Workflows event card; the constraint is active-flow tiers
A Group Rule; the constraint is that it cannot call external systems
An Event Hook; the constraint is the 400,000 events per day limit
An Inline Hook; the constraint is that Okta waits only about three seconds for a response
questions.explanation: Only Inline Hooks are synchronous: Okta pauses the transaction and waits for your answer. The documented timeout is three seconds, so any external lookup must be fast or pre-cached. Event Hooks and Workflows event cards are asynchronous and cannot modify the transaction.

questions.stem: Where does the data that moves from an Okta "User Created" event card into a Slack "Send Message" card come from?
options: The flow's table, which caches event payloads
Mapping: dragging the event card's output fields onto the action card's input fields
A JSON expression typed into the Slack card
A variable you declare at the top of the flow
questions.explanation: Workflows has no variables in the programming sense. Every card exposes outputs, and you map an output onto a later card's input by drag and drop. Tables are for state between executions, not for passing data within one.

questions.stem: An auditor asks what identity performed the deactivations your flows carried out last month. What determines the answer?
options: A built-in "Okta Workflows" system actor, always
The admin who clicked Run on the flow
The account used to authorise the Okta connection the flow uses
The owner of the folder the flow lives in
questions.explanation: The Okta connection is authorised by a real account, and actions through that connection are attributed to it. That is why Okta recommends a dedicated service account with super admin rights for the connection, rather than whichever admin happened to set it up.
